title: the rains
hook: a new king forgets, a counselor remembers, and autumn arrives

segments.voice: Yesterday: the rains, and Rama's monsoon poem of viraha, love in separation. Looking slows him down.

Down in Kishkindha, the new king is having a wonderful time, and Valmiki doesn't hide it. Sugriva has his kingdom back after years on the run. He has his wife Ruma back, and Tara is in the palace as his queen as well. He spends the season in comfort, feasting and drinking, with music in the halls. Up on the mountain, the rain falls on a cave. Then the rains end. The sky clears. And Sugriva hasn't noticed.
screen: `A WONDERFUL TIME IN KISHKINDHA.` → `MUSIC IN THE HALLS.` → `THE RAINS END, UNNOTICED.`

segments.voice: Hanuman notices. He goes to Sugriva first, before anyone gets angry, and speaks the way he always does, carefully. You have your kingdom, he says. You have your glory. Now it's time to help your friends. Rama helped you; it's your turn. A king who forgets a friend's service when the time comes loses everyone's respect. Don't wait to be asked. Sugriva hears him, and orders his commanders to gather the monkey armies from every mountain and forest within fifteen days. Friendship sometimes needs a reminder, and the best one comes early and gently, from someone who cares about both sides. Meanwhile the season turns. Autumn arrives, sharad, and Valmiki turns to a new kind of description. Rivers clear and slow down and show their sandbanks. The sky is clean and blue. Cranes fly. Lotuses open. Roads are passable again: the season kings set out. For Rama, autumn is an alarm. Up on Prasravana he looks at the clear sky and knows the waiting time is over, and there's no word from Sugriva. He has been patient for four months. Now he begins to wonder whether his friend has forgotten him entirely. Tomorrow, Rama sends a message, and he sends it by his brother, who is not in a gentle mood.
screen: `HANUMAN REMINDS SUGRIVA.` · `ARMIES ORDERED IN FIFTEEN DAYS.` · `SHARAD: AUTUMN'S CLEAR SKY.` · `RAMA HEARS NO WORD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who did something for you that you haven't returned yet, not to feel guilty, just to remember. Breathe in and see their face; breathe out and let one small way to repay them come to mind. Then let the plan go and simply breathe, the way a clear autumn sky simply is.
The rains. They end in a clear autumn sky, Hanuman's early reminder, and Rama wondering whether his friend forgot.
Your line: don't wait to be asked. Hanuman spoke up before anyone got angry. That's day five hundred ninety.

howItsDone: Autumn (sharad) opens the Hindu festival season, with Navaratri and Dussehra; in some regions Dussehra celebrates Rama's victory (in others, Durga's), and Ramlila performances are staged in the weeks around it.
